title: Multiple Mixture Responses (same model formula) Optimizer
labelAnalysisTime: Be patient! Optimization may take longer with more responses, more mixture components, or more random restarts.
response: Select one or more response (dependent) variables -- one Scheffe model of the same type is fit for each response automatically, no pre-existing model needed
lblModelType: Model Type (applied identically to every selected response)
linearChk: Linear Scheffé model — main effects only
quadChk: Quadratic Scheffé model — main effects + all pairwise component interactions
cubicChk: Special Cubic Scheffé model — quadratic + all three-way component products
lblModelTypeNote: Full Cubic Scheffé models are not supported. Because every response is fit with this same model type over the same components, all selected responses automatically share an identical model formula -- no separate compatibility check is needed.
instructionLabel: Specify comma-separated values -- one value for each response, in the same order selected above
goal: Goal: (Specify minimize, maximize, target, or range)
target: Target: Specify target values of the responses
lower: Lower: Specify minimum acceptable values of the responses (if left blank, that response's own fitted-value range is used)
upper: Upper: Specify maximum acceptable values of the responses (if left blank, that response's own fitted-value range is used)
weight: Weight: Specify weight values (penalty for being away from target); must be > 0, default 1
importance: Importance: Specify importance for combining multiple responses; must be > 0, default 1
totalAmount: Total amount (components must sum to this value, in the same units as the bounds below)
lowerBoundsInput: Lower bounds (optional -- comma-separated, one per component, in the SAME order shown above)
upperBoundsInput: Upper bounds (optional -- comma-separated, one per component, in the SAME order shown above)
lblBoundsNote: Optional. Leave BOTH fields blank to automatically use the minimum and maximum of each component observed in the dataset. This works reliably for designs where the true bounds are actually reached by at least one run -- Simplex Lattice, Simplex Centroid, and Extreme Vertices designs all guarantee this by construction. WARNING: for a D-optimal-selected design, auto-derived bounds may be unreliable -- D-optimal point selection is not guaranteed to touch every true extreme, so the derived range could be narrower than actually intended. If your design came from a D-optimal search, specify both bounds explicitly to guide the optimization correctly.
numOfStartsNote: The search is a smooth local optimizer (optim, L-BFGS-B) applied to the mixture's free components, with the last component always computed from the sum-to-Total constraint. Multiple random restarts (default 20) reduce the chance of settling on a local rather than global optimum.
randomseedsNote: Optional. Leave blank to use a different random starting configuration each time you run this (results may vary slightly run-to-run, since the restarts beyond the first are randomly generated). Specify a number for reproducible, identical results every time you re-run with the same inputs.
showModelFormulaChk: Show model formula for each response
showCoefficientsChk: Show coefficient table for each response
showEachModelPredictionChk: Show predicted response and individual desirability for each response at the optimum
saveModelChk: Save each fitted model (as MixModel_<response>) for later use with the Model Evaluation menu

help.title: Optimize Multiple Mixture Responses, Same Model Formula (Desirability)
help.r_help: help(optim, package = stats); help(lm, package = stats)
help.body:
Description
Fits a Scheffé canonical mixture model (Linear, Quadratic, or Special Cubic) directly from the active dataset for EACH selected response variable, then finds the mixture composition that best satisfies all of them simultaneously via a Derringer-Suich composite desirability function. No pre-existing model from Analyze Mixture Design is required -- exactly one model, using the same model type, is built automatically per response, matching how this suite's general-purpose Multiple Response (same model formula) Optimizer builds one lm() per response internally rather than requiring an already-fit model to be selected.

Why the general-purpose response optimizers don't work for mixtures
This suite's general-purpose response optimizers search using optim(method = "L-BFGS-B", lower =, upper =) -- independent box constraints on every predictor, with no way to express an equality constraint like A+B+C+D = Total. Given a mixture model, that search would happily evaluate points like A=40, B=40, C=40, D=40 (summing to 160), meaningless for a model only ever valid on the constrained simplex it was fit on. This dialog instead parameterizes the search over only q-1 free components, always computing the last component as Total minus the sum of the others, so every candidate point evaluated sums to Total exactly.

Why mixture models have no intercept
Because mixture components always sum to a fixed total, an ordinary intercept term is mathematically redundant — Scheffé canonical models omit it. This dialog fits models of exactly this no-intercept form automatically for every response.

Mixture Setup
Total amount and component bounds must be supplied directly (in the same units the response data was collected in) -- there is no existing design dataset here to derive bounds from automatically, unlike Augment Mixture Design.

Composite Desirability
D = (d1^w1 x d2^w2 x ... )^(1/sum(w)), the geometric mean of each response's individual desirability (0 to 1), weighted by Importance. D = 0 if any single response completely fails its goal; D = 1 only if every response fully meets its goal simultaneously.
